newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIA'S KROELL DIES IN CAR CRASH.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIA'S KROELL DIES IN CAR CRASH.

text.p: Austrian World Cup ski racer Richard Kroell was killed in a traffic accident on Saturday afternoon when his car crashed into an oncoming bus, the Austrian news agency APA reported.
The fatal accident was reported to have occurred in the Zillertal valley near Kroell's hometown of Grizning in the western Austrian province of Tyrol. Officials said the 28-year-old died on the spot.
Kroell, who leaves behind his wife and a daughter, joined the Austrian ski team in 1984.

In 1990, he captured his maiden World Cup victories on two of the most demanding giant slalom slopes on the circuit in Alta Badia, Italy and Veysonnaz, Switzerland. In the same year, he was overall fourth in the giant slalom standings.

After four unsuccessful years, he made a comeback to the elite of ski racing in 1995 by winning a super-g in Bormio, Italy and completing the winter in overall sixth place in the discipline's standings.
Kroell had spent the past few weeks training with the Austrian team on a glacier at Soelden, site of the World Cup season's opening race, a giant slalom, on October 27.
A number of Austrian skiers have died in the last six years.

In 1991, Gernot Reinstadler was killed during a training run for a World Cup downhill race in Wengen, Switzerland and double World Champion Rudolf Nierlich died in a car accident. One year later, Peter Wirnsberger II died from injuries sustained during a fall during free skiing in Austria.

In 1994, two-time World Champion Ulrike Maier died in a World Cup downhill at Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany and Christoph Laimer, a member of the junior team, was killed in an accident during free skiing on an Austrian glacier.
